public_sources.bound_semantics: Kleinberg, Niculescu-Mizil and Sharma study online decision problems in which the set of actions available to the decision algorithm varies over time, including partial-information multi-armed bandits.

UCB1 initializes each available machine once and thereafter compares current average reward plus sqrt(2 ln n/n_j); in this reduction that index arithmetic is reused only after exact active-set filtering.

chat_native_reduction.mapping: Persist a time-varying exact eligible assignment set. Optimize only over that set; sleeping assignments retain prior same-scope accepted statistics but acquire no reward/count while inactive. Eligibility transitions allocate a fresh generation fence so late completions cannot act as current evidence.
chat_native_reduction.new_arm_rule: A newly active assignment with zero accepted observations receives one bounded initialization probe before UCB index comparison, matching the already validated UCB1 initialization principle.
chat_native_reduction.theorem_scope: Sleeping-bandit regret bounds and UCB1 stochastic regret assumptions are not claimed for this deterministic role-local trace.
